science.title: Mathematical modeling and cross-salt validation of layer-by-layer deposition of cadmium sulfide thin films: correlating thickness, morphology, and functional relevance from sensor to photocatalytic ap
science.description: The paper presents a systematic study of the layer-by-layer chemical deposition of cadmium sulfide thin films. The research aimed to establish relationships among concentration parameters, the number of deposition cycles, morphological characteristics, and functional properties. The objective of the study was to develop a mathematical model to quantitatively describe film growth kinetics and predict film thickness from process parameters. A multifactor regression analysis was employed, with model coefficients determined using the least-squares method in matrix form. The construction of the design matrices enabled the inclusion of primary variables, as well as interaction and quadratic terms that capture the nonlinear nature of film growth. This approach ensured high accuracy in approximating experimental data and yielded a statistically significant model capable of reproducing and predicting deposition trends. The model’s reliability was verified through cross-salt validation, in which analogous deposition conditions were applied with various cadmium sources, including sulfate, chloride, iodide, nitrate, and acetate. The comparative analysis confirmed that the fundamental growth patterns are preserved across different salt-system compositions, demonstrating the model’s universality and transferability across various technological environments. To better understand film-forming patterns, 3D visualization of both experimental and modeled data was performed, enabling the spatial relationships among reagent concentration, the number of deposition cycles, and film thickness to be traced. The visualization confirmed the adequacy of the chosen model. The optical and morphological characteristics of the obtained films were analyzed, revealing that variations in film thickness directly influence the transmittance coefficient and the bandgap (Eg). Thinner films exhibited high optical transparency, potentially relevant to sensing and optoelectronic applications, whereas thicker films showed enhanced optical absorption.

science.title: Caffeine-related exposure and dry eye disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological associations and tear-related outcomes
science.description: Caffeine intake has been described as a potential lifestyle factor in dry eye disease (DED), but evidence remains conflicting. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between caffeine-related exposure and DED and summarized clinical studies examining tear-film parameters. Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Twenty-three studies were included: 14 epidemiological studies involving 117,736 participants and 9 tear-parameter studies involving 519 participants. Grouped analysis without separating caffeine sources showed no significant association with DED and substantial heterogeneity (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74–1.08; I² = 69%). Heterogeneity decreased in adjusted estimates (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80–1.05; I² = 40%). After excluding the tea-specific study, the remaining adjusted studies showed a significant inverse association (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.75–0.96; I² = 0%). Tear-parameter studies suggested transient increases in tear secretion after pure caffeine, while beverage-based effects on tear stability were inconsistent. In summary, current evidence does not establish caffeine-related exposure as protective against DED. Future studies should distinguish caffeine from beverage constituents and evaluate topical caffeine or methylxanthine analogues.
